To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed three software applications, BugMat, FindNeighbour and the server version of FindNeighbour, that generate bacterial distance matrices, that we have shown these applications can be scaled up to handle thousands of bacterial isolates, and that we have shown the applications can handle a range of different types of bacterial genomes.

we developed three applications for the analysis of large collections of bacterial sequences, each with distinct advantages and disadvantages, and that we deployed these as part of a solution for the analysis of M. tuberculosis genomic data.
we developed, tested, and deployed three applications for distance-matrix analysis of large bacterial genomic sequence collections.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing tools for the analysis of large-scale genomic data, and we have shown how the use of reference genomes and compression techniques allows the generation of large, sparse distance matrices.
the development and deployment of software for the rapid and accurate analysis of bacterial genomic sequences.
the generation and maintenance, and the use, of distance matrices for bacterial genomic analysis.

BugMat and FindNeighbours are all useful tools for the generation and maintenance, respectively, of large bacterial distance matrices.

BugMat is the fastest application, FindNeighbour2 is the most scalable, and FindNeighbour is the most flexible.

we have provided three applications for generating distance matrices, each of which is fast and scalable to large numbers of bacterial genomes, and which are available to the public for download and use.
